The test image shows an open soybean pod held in hand with:
- Left pod half: shrunken/aborted seed with dark brown discoloration
- Right pod half: one normal yellow seed + one shrunken/wrinkled seed with dark markings
- Pod walls are tan/brown, somewhat damaged

Top candidates: **Phomopsis** (seed decay), **Diaporthe** (pod & stem blight), **Purple_Seed_Stain**. Let me compare reference images.

Key observations from references:
- **Phomopsis**: Shows shrunken/aborted seeds in pods, pod lesions with pycnidia — very similar to test image
- **Diaporthe**: Primarily stem cankers and plant dieback — doesn't match
- **Purple_Seed_Stain**: Shows purple/dark blotches on otherwise normal seeds — doesn't match (test seeds are shrunken/aborted, not stained)

Let me check one more candidate to be thorough.

**Anthracnose** reference shows external pod lesions (dark blotches on pod exterior) and mass pod shriveling on plants — doesn't match the interior seed decay pattern in the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: open soybean pod showing shrunken/aborted seeds with dark discoloration — classic **Phomopsis seed decay**
- Phomopsis reference directly shows this pattern: shrunken/chalky seeds in pods, tan pod walls
- Diaporthe = stem cankers (no match); Purple_Seed_Stain = purple-stained normal-sized seeds (no match); Anthracnose = exterior pod lesions/mass shriveling (no match)
